svg.title: Two angle diagrams with equations and missing measures
svg.desc: Left panel: an upper half-plane at point P is partitioned by two rays into adjacent angles 40 degrees, x degrees, and x degrees, in that order from the horizontal right ray toward the horizontal left ray. They form a straight angle: 40 plus x plus x equals 180, so x equals 70 degrees. Right panel: two straight lines meet at Q. An upper-right angle of 70 degrees is vertically opposite a lower-left angle labeled 3y plus 10 degrees. Their equality gives 3y plus 10 equals 70, so y equals 20. The drawings are independently authored examples, not publisher graphics. Learners should explain how the diagrams support each equation.
svg.text: Use the angle relationships to write and solve an equation
A. Three parts of a straight angle
B. A pair of vertical angles
Original Edulytiks models. Explain the straight-angle or vertical-angle justification before using the equation.
